parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the *centre of gravity* of a body.

markscheme_points.text: point where (all) the weight (of the object) is considered/seems to act

hints: Hint 1: Think of the weight of a body as made up of lots of tiny weights acting on every particle - where could a single force replace all of them?
Hint 2: Focus your definition on the word point and link it clearly to the total weight acting at that one place.
parts.proper_answer: The centre of gravity is the point where the whole weight of the body may be considered to act.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Picture Weight Acting Everywhere**
Every part of the post has a tiny gravitational pull on it. Added together, all these tiny pulls give the total weight of $45\text{ N}$. It would be very awkward to draw hundreds of arrows, so in physics you replace them with one single arrow.

Step 2: **Define The Special Point**
That single arrow is drawn from a special point called the centre of gravity. So you can say: $$ \text{centre of gravity = point where total weight is considered to act} $$ For a uniform post, this is at its midpoint.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem:
A uniform wooden post AB of weight $45\text{ N}$ stands in equilibrium on hard ground, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

{{figure:figure_2_1}}

Fig. 2.1 (not to scale)

End A of the vertical post is supported by the ground. A horizontal wire with tension $T$ is attached to end B of the post. Another wire, attached to the post at point C, is at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ to the horizontal and has tension $38\text{ N}$. The distances along the post of points A, B and C are shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the horizontal component of the force exerted on the post by the wire connected to point C.

markscheme_points.text: horizontal component of force = 38 cos 60° = 19 N

hints: Hint 1: The 38 N wire makes 60 degrees with the horizontal, so sketch its horizontal and vertical arrows and decide which side of the triangle is adjacent to the 60 degree angle.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Resolve Along The Horizontal**
The wire pulls at $60^{\circ}$ below the horizontal. Its effect to the side is the adjacent side of the force triangle, while the full $38\text{ N}$ is the hypotenuse.

Step 2: **Calculate The Component**
Using cosine for adjacent over hypotenuse: $$ F_h = 38 \cos 60^{\circ} $$ $$ F_h = 19\text{ N} $$ This acts to the right, balancing the tension $T$ to the left.

key_concepts: horizontal component adjacent to given angle

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: By considering moments about end A, determine the tension $T$.
hints: Hint 1: Take moments about A so the unknown forces at A have zero moment, then decide which of T, the 45 N weight and the 38 N wire actually tend to turn the post about A.
Hint 2: Remember the post is in equilibrium, so the anticlockwise moment from T must balance the clockwise moment from the horizontal push at C, using the heights 1.20 m and 0.90 m from A.
parts.proper_answer: Taking moments about A, $T \times 1.20 = 19 \times 0.90$, giving $T = 14\text{ N}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Choose A To Remove Unknowns**
Taking moments about end A is clever because any force at A has zero perpendicular distance from A, so its moment is zero. The $45\text{ N}$ weight acts straight down through the post, so its line passes through A and it also has zero moment about A.

Step 2: **Write Clockwise Equals Anticlockwise**
Tension $T$ acts left at height $0.90 + 0.30 = 1.20\text{ m}$ above A. It tends to turn the post anticlockwise. The horizontal $19\text{ N}$ from part (i) acts right at height $0.90\text{ m}$ above A. It tends to turn the post clockwise. For equilibrium: $$ \text{sum of moments about A} = 0 $$ $$ T \times 1.20 = 19 \times 0.90 $$

Step 3: **Solve For T**
$$ T = \frac{19 \times 0.90}{1.20} $$ $$ T = 14\text{ N} \text{ (to 2 s.f.)} $$

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the vertical component of the force exerted on the post at end A.
hints: Hint 1: Think vertically - the ground must push up at A to balance all the downward pulls from the weight of the post and the downward pull of the angled wire.
parts.proper_answer: Vertical force at A $= 45 + 38 \sin 60^{\circ} = 78\text{ N}$ upwards.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Balance Forces Vertically**
In equilibrium the total upward force equals the total downward force. Downwards you have the $45\text{ N}$ weight plus the vertical part of the $38\text{ N}$ wire pull. Upwards you have only the push from the ground at A, call it $F$.

Step 2: **Add The Downward Components**
The vertical component is opposite the $60^{\circ}$ angle, so it uses sine: $$ F = 45 + 38 \sin 60^{\circ} $$ $$ F = 45 + 32.9 = 78\text{ N} $$ This is the upward vertical component exerted by the ground on the post at A.
